# Allowed combinations by dtype
#
# Polars: the release py-2.1.0 at the commit 7f902bd3ffd27ff82d14278a09a295ff2f7aed92 of vendor/polars.
# Generated from the catalogue and Polars by the engine test
# `allowed::tests::artifacts::the_committed_tables_are_what_polars_gives`, with Polars on
# one thread, so that a reason that depends on which of two failures comes first is the
# same every time. Do not edit.
# To refresh after a change of the catalogue or of Polars:
#   DAGEIST_REFRESH_TABLES=1 cargo test --offline --locked -p dageist-engine allowed::tests::artifacts
# See docs/how-to.md, "Refresh The Tables Of Allowed Combinations".
#
# Each line is: entry | parameter | receiver | argument | outcome.
#
# An expression method is run in `select` on a column `a` of the receiver dtype. With
# `-` for the parameter and the argument, every parameter is at its default. Otherwise
# the parameter is given a column `b` of the argument dtype, or, where Polars takes one
# value only (`shift`'s `n` and `fill_value`), the number 1 of that dtype, and the others are at
# their defaults. `over` is given `partition_by` unless that or `order_by` is the
# parameter, each of which it takes alone, and `*more_exprs` extends `partition_by`. A
# cast is given the dtype of its receiver. A replacement is given what it replaces and
# what replaces it, a column `a` of the receiver's dtype for the one that is not tested,
# and a strict one a default, `a` where `old` is tested and `b` otherwise, so that a value
# it does not list is not refused; an interval is given `a` for the bound that is not
# tested. The columns hold three rows: a value, a null and a value. Text is a duration in
# days, such as `1d`.
#
# An outcome is `allowed <dtype of the result> <one|many>` (`-` for a step), or
# `refused <stage>: <Polars' reason>`. A combination is allowed only when Polars resolved
# its schema, ran it on three rows that include a null, and ran it on a table with no rows.
# The stage is where Polars refused it: `schema`; `rows`, when the schema resolved and
# the rows were refused; or `empty`, when only the table with no rows was. `one` is a
# value for the three rows together, `many` any other number. A reason is Polars' message
# up to its first blank line, on one line.
#
# 46254 combinations: 15198 allowed; 7516 refused when Polars resolved the schema, 23540 when it ran the rows, 0 when it ran the empty table.
#
